consensus_issues.description: format-speedup can produce exact rational fractions (e.g., '33/10') instead of decimal strings in many Scheme implementations (like R5RS/Chez). This affects the professional formatting and readability of the analysis reports.
consensus_issues.suggested_fix: Coerce the value to an inexact number using (exact->inexact) or multiply by 1.0 before formatting to ensure decimal output (e.g., (/ (round (* (exact->inexact s) 10)) 10)).

consensus_issues.description: 'truncate-expr' generates a full string representation of an expression via 'format ~s' before truncating. For large nested expressions, this can cause significant performance hits and memory pressure.
consensus_issues.suggested_fix: Use a bounded printer or check the depth/complexity of the expression before stringification to avoid processing massive trees.

lattice/fp/analysis/fusion-detect.ss.description: Performance bottleneck in fusion-detect-at-depth: uses (append acc child-opps) inside a loop. This results in O(N^2) complexity relative to the number of detected opportunities, which can be slow for very large expressions or deeply nested ASTs.
lattice/fp/analysis/fusion-detect.ss.code_snippet:
(let loop ([items expr] [i 0] [acc '()])
     (if (or (null? items) (not (pair? items)))
         acc
         (let ([child-opps (fusion-detect-at-depth ...)])
              (loop (cdr items) (+ i 1) (append acc child-opps)))))
lattice/fp/analysis/fusion-detect.ss.suggested_fix: Accumulate results in a flat list using a single pass or use a more efficient data structure (like a difference list or simple consing followed by a single reverse).

lattice/fp/analysis/parallel-detect.ss.description: Critical bug in free variable analysis: misses free variables in zero-argument functions and empty binding forms. The (pair? (cadr expr)) check incorrectly skips forms like (lambda () body) and (let () body), returning an empty list of free variables and potentially leading to unsafe parallelization suggestions.
lattice/fp/analysis/parallel-detect.ss.suggested_fix: Change (pair? (cadr expr)) to (list? (cadr expr)) or simply check (pair? (cdr expr)) to allow empty parameter/binding lists. Ensure the logic handles the empty case correctly by still recursing into the body.

lattice/fp/analysis/parallel-detect.ss.description: Named let forms are not supported in free-vars-env. When (car expr) is 'let and (cadr expr) is a symbol (the loop name), the (pair? (cadr expr)) check fails, and the form returns an empty free variable list. This causes the analyzer to miss all free variables in the bindings and body of named loops.
lattice/fp/analysis/parallel-detect.ss.suggested_fix: Add a branch to handle named let: (and (symbol? (cadr expr)) (pair? (cddr expr))). Extract bindings from (caddr expr) and body from (cdddr expr).

lattice/fp/analysis/parallel-detect.ss.description: Incomplete independence check in detect-independent-maps: it only analyzes the free variables of the data (the third argument to map), completely ignoring the mapping function (the second argument). If two maps use independent data but share a stateful or effectful function, they will be incorrectly marked as safe for parallelization.
lattice/fp/analysis/parallel-detect.ss.suggested_fix: Include the function expression in the free variable analysis: (map (lambda (m) (append (free-vars (cadr m)) (free-vars (caddr m)))) map-exprs).

lattice/fp/rewrite/verify.ss.description: Namespace pollution: verify.ss defines a broken and incomplete version of free-vars that shadows the more comprehensive one in parallel-detect.ss. Since verify.ss is loaded later in shell/lzr.ss, the parallelization analysis ends up using this restricted version which only supports single-argument 'fn' forms and basic 'let'.
lattice/fp/rewrite/verify.ss.suggested_fix: Rename this local version to verify-free-vars or move both to a shared module. In a non-module system, use a prefix to avoid collisions between analysis and verification passes.

lattice/fp/rewrite/verify.ss.description: Bug in substitute: the shadowing check only looks at the first parameter of a function. In a multi-argument function (fn (x y) body), if 'y' is the variable being substituted, it will incorrectly substitute inside the body even though 'y' is shadowed by the parameter list.
lattice/fp/rewrite/verify.ss.suggested_fix: Use (memq var (cadr expr)) instead of (eq? (caadr expr) var) to check for shadowing in the entire parameter list.

shell/debug/session-debug.ss.description: test-session-state assumes all session fields ('name, 'tier, 'login-time) are always present in the alist returned by read-session. If any are missing, assq returns #f and cdr will raise an exception.
shell/debug/session-debug.ss.code_snippet:
(display (format "  Name: ~a
" (cdr (assq 'name session))))
(display (format "  Tier: ~a
" (cdr (assq 'tier session))))
(display (format "  Login time: ~a
" (cdr (assq 'login-time session))))
shell/debug/session-debug.ss.suggested_fix: Use a helper to safely access alist values. Example: (define (session-ref s k) (let ([p (assq k s)]) (if p (cdr p) "unknown")))

shell/lzr.ss.description: Shadowing of 'detect-at-depth' causes stale binding issues. Saving 'detect-fusion-static' into '*lzr-fusion-detect*' does not prevent its internal calls from using the redefined version of 'detect-at-depth' from 'parallel-detect.ss' because Scheme top-level definitions are late-bound.
shell/lzr.ss.suggested_fix: Use a module system to encapsulate dependencies or rename internal functions to ensure uniqueness. If using 'load', ensure that internal helpers like 'detect-at-depth' are not redefined by subsequent loads.

shell/lzr.ss.description: 'worth-optimizing?' lacks guards for non-pair expressions, unlike other API functions such as 'analyze-fusion' and 'suggest-parallel'. Passing a symbol or null to this function will likely cause a crash in the underlying detection functions.
'lzr-report' performs redundant optimization work by calling both 'optimize' and 'optimize-with-stats', both of which execute the same fusion simplification logic.
shell/lzr.ss.suggested_fix: Extract the 'result' from the 'stats' alist (returned by 'optimize-with-stats') instead of calling 'optimize' separately.

shell/lzr.ss.description: 'analyze-all' computes summary statistics ('fusion-sum' and 'parallel-sum') that are never utilized by 'lzr-report' or the display logic, resulting in unnecessary computation.
shell/lzr.ss.suggested_fix: Remove the unused summary calculations or integrate them into the final report output.

shell/lzr.ss.description: verify-rewrite and test-with-samples in shell/lzr.ss are likely to produce false negatives because verify-equivalence only checks for alpha-equivalence. Since fusion and parallelization optimizations naturally change the structure of the expression, they will rarely be alpha-equivalent to the original, making the verification pass almost always fail.
shell/lzr.ss.suggested_fix: The verification should involve symbolic evaluation or NbE (Normalization by Evaluation) as hinted in verify.ss comments, or test-with-samples should actually evaluate the expressions with the provided inputs and compare results.

shell/lzr.ss.description: test-with-samples performs structural comparison using verify-equivalence after substitution but does not evaluate the expressions. This causes it to fail for semantically equivalent but structurally different expressions (e.g., fused vs. unfused forms), making it ineffective for verifying rewrites with sample data.
shell/lzr.ss.code_snippet:
(define (test-with-samples before after sample-inputs)
  (let* ([before-sub (substitute-all before sample-inputs)]
         [after-sub (substitute-all after sample-inputs)]
         [result (verify-equivalence before-sub after-sub)])
shell/lzr.ss.suggested_fix: Use an evaluator (e.g., eval) to compare the resulting values of the expressions after substitution instead of using structural/alpha equivalence.

shell/lzr.ss.description: substitute-all implements sequential substitution instead of simultaneous substitution. This produces incorrect results when substitution values contain variables that are also being replaced (e.g., swapping variables 'x' and 'y' will result in both becoming the same value).
shell/lzr.ss.code_snippet:
(define (substitute-all expr bindings)
  (if (null? bindings)
      expr
      (substitute-all (substitute expr (caar bindings) (cdar bindings))
                      (cdr bindings))))
shell/lzr.ss.suggested_fix: Implement a simultaneous substitution function that determines all replacements before applying them to the expression.

shell/lzr.ss.description: The percent-reduction calculation in optimize-with-stats can result in an exact rational fraction (e.g., 100/3), which will be displayed as a fraction in the final report instead of a formatted percentage.
shell/lzr.ss.suggested_fix: Ensure the division result is inexact by using (exact->inexact) or 100.0 to produce a decimal percentage.

shell/repl/eval-repl.ss.description: fold-type-string extracts a substitution from the context but fails to apply it to the typed-result, contradicting the intent stated in the comment and likely displaying an un-unified/internal type representation.
shell/repl/eval-repl.ss.code_snippet:
(if (and (pair? context)
         (pair? (car context))
         (eq? (caar context) 'substitution))
    ;; Extract and apply substitution to get final type
    (let ([subst (cadar context)])
         (write typed-result)
         (newline))
shell/repl/eval-repl.ss.suggested_fix: Call a type substitution application function (e.g., apply-substitution) on typed-result before writing it. Example: (write (apply-substitution typed-result subst))

shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.description: Potential crash in store-stats when the store is empty. compute-store-stats returns an alist without tag-distribution or ref-distribution keys if total-blocks is 0, causing cdr to be called on #f.
shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.code_snippet:
(let ([tag-dist (cdr (assq 'tag-distribution stats))])
     (display "Tag Distribution:\n")
     (let ([tags (list-sort
                  (lambda (a b) (> (cdr a) (cdr b)))
                  (hashtable-map tag-dist cons))])
shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.suggested_fix: Add a check for the existence of the keys or ensure compute-store-stats returns empty distributions. Example: (let ([tag-dist (cond [(assq 'tag-distribution stats) => cdr] [else '()])]))

shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.description: hash->hex uses string-set! on a string that may be immutable. It is created via a redefined make-string which uses list->string; in many Scheme implementations (like Racket), list->string produces immutable strings.
shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.code_snippet:
(let* ([len (bytevector-length hash)]
       [hex-chars (make-string (* len 2) #\0)])
      (let loop ([i 0])
           (when (< i len)
                 (let ([byte (bytevector-u8-ref hash i)])
                      (string-set! hex-chars (* i 2) (int->hex-digit (quotient byte 16)))
                      (string-set! hex-chars (+ (* i 2) 1) (int->hex-digit (remainder byte 16)))
                      (loop (+ i 1)))))
shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.suggested_fix: Use the standard make-string (ensure it's not shadowed) which usually creates mutable strings, or use a bytevector and then convert to string, or use string-append/format to build the hex string.

shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.description: Redefinition of standard make-string procedure using an inefficient and non-tail-recursive make-list-of. This shadows the built-in optimized make-string and may cause stack overflow for large n.
shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.code_snippet:
(define (make-string n ch)
  (list->string (make-list-of n ch)))

(define (make-list-of n x)
  (if (= n 0)
      '()
      (cons x (make-list-of (- n 1) x))))
shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.suggested_fix: Remove the redefinition and use the built-in make-string. If a custom version is needed, implement it using a loop and string-set! or a tail-recursive list builder.

shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.description: find-broken-refs uses append in a loop to accumulate results. This leads to O(N^2) complexity in the number of broken references, which can be significant in a corrupted large store.
shell/storage/store-analyze.ss.suggested_fix: Accumulate results using cons and reverse the final list at the end of the loop, or use a more efficient list builder.
